transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As we all know, we want to preserve several of our older relatives' stories in recordings that future family members can listen to and watch. I've got the only working camcorder, so I'm coordinating the recording evening and will decide how the files are handled afterward. We've got the family shared digital drive available for storing everything once we're done. Before I finalize the plan, I want to hear from each of you individually — Nina, then Omar — about any preferences, advice, or constraints you have regarding the recording setup or file handling. Please go ahead and share whatever's on your mind, and I'll record your responses before making my final decisions.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important — my grandmother told me she's willing to be recorded only if the interviews stay in the family archive and are not posted publicly online. I haven't mentioned this to anyone yet, but I think it's important we factor this into the plan before finalizing anything.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I want to share some advice I got from my friend Priya, who's an audiovisual archivist. She recommended that we capture the audio as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and that we make two verified backup copies. I haven't had a chance to bring this up until now, but I think it's important we factor these specs into the recording and file-handling plan before finalizing anything.
transcript.speaker: A3
